correctness.rationale: For n>=4, a mixed pair observes all but at most two vertices after the closed-neighborhood step and one-observed-neighbor forcing completes it; a pure r-set with r>=2 observes B and can force the n-r unseen same-shore vertices iff n-r<=2. A singleton stalls. The iff classification yields the two polynomials by direct shore selection and the minimal sizes 2,n-2. At TAR budget 2 all n^2 mixed pairs are isolated (n=4 additionally 12 pure pairs); at budget>=3 pairs exchange via an added token; at budget n-2 each minimal pure (n-2)-set is an isolated new vertex, and at n-1 adding one opposite-shore token joins every pure set. Verified n=4,5,6 independently by exhaustive domination and budget components; this is a finite cross-check, not the n-unbounded proof.
